text:
Rhea Menon: Halo Health asked in the RFI whether we can offer a 'partner-burst' option for POC so overflow goes to a partner cloud (FedRAMP-equivalent) instead of our public hosted pool. They want the exact behavior and a short procurement-safe line.

Kai Brooks: Short answer: yes, for qualifying customers we can route overflow to a vetted partner region via an interconnect/peering. Add a capability row: 'Dedicated primary + partner-burst (opt-in)'. Note: partner-burst requires contract with partner and network setup.

Jonah Park: Important callouts for the RFI: 1) Data residency preserved inside partner region, 2) fallback is region-restricted and audited, 3) partner processing uses partner-managed keys unless customer supplies cross-account KMS.

security-bot: RFI text suggestion: "Partner-burst routes overflow traffic only to a pre-approved partner tenancy in specified regions; payloads are encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest per partner controls. Enabling partner-burst requires signed partner addendum and network peering. Audit logs recorded for burst actions and retained 540 days."

Rhea Menon: Procurement wants one-line procurement-safe phrasing they can paste. Any ideas?

Kai Brooks: "Overflow may be routed to an approved partner tenancy in the Customer's region upon Customer election and execution of the Partner-Burst Addendum; Redwood is not liable for partner-managed processing where Customer has authorized Partner-Burst in writing."

BillingAgent: Pricing note for RFI table: partner-burst unit rate = hosted-overflow rate + partner surcharge (typical +20%-40%). POC baseline (Dedicated 2x mid-GPU): $17,000/mo. Example: if 10% of traffic overflows to partner, estimated add +$3.6k/mo (assumes partner surcharge 30%). Add cell: 'Cost delta (example 10% partner overflow): +$3.6k (+21%)'.

Jonah Park: Also list worst-case for budgeting: 48h at 60% partner overflow -> approx +$8.2k that month. Put cell: 'Worst-case (48h,60%): +$8.2k (+48%)'.

Rhea Menon: They asked for an ops snippet showing how partner-burst is enabled/disabled so infra can vet. Keep tiny.

Kai Brooks: ```json
{
  "project":"halo-poc",
  "routing_policy":{
    "primary":"dedicated-halo",
    "partner_burst_enabled":true,
    "partner_tenancy":"partner-fedramp-eu",
    "conditions":["cluster_util>0.85","p99>300ms"],
    "drain_seconds":300
  }
}
```

Rhea Menon: Good. Security also asked for proof artifacts to attach. Jonah, can you attach the partner's accreditation excerpt and our redacted network diagram?

Jonah Park: Uploaded both: https://files.redwood.internal/sales/halo/partner_accreditation_excerpt.pdf and https://files.redwood.internal/sales/halo/network_peering_sketch.png :paperclip:

security-bot: Also include: "Audit events exported via S3/syslog or pushed to customer SIEM; partner activity tags included in logs."

BillingAgent: Addendum note for procurement cell: "Partner-Burst Addendum required; partner costs billed via Redwood as pass-through or direct invoicing per contract."

Rhea Menon: Final ask: one short SLA line for the RFI POC section. Jonah?

Jonah Park: "During the POC, Redwood guarantees 99.5% availability of Dedicated capacity; partner-burst availability and latency are provided by the partner and estimated in the appendix."

Rhea Menon: Perfect. I'll fold these rows into the capability matrix, attach artifacts, and send to Halo by EOD. Scheduling follow-up call with their security lead tomorrow 11am PT. :white_check_mark:
